author: val
body: handoff-magic is the eight ASCII bytes "CDXHANDF" read as one little-endian quadword, which is how the stub stores them.

author: val
body: A zero base now means what it says. The stub writes the header unconditionally but jumps over the framebuffer body when LocateProtocol(GOP) returned nothing, so callers must still treat a zero base as "no framebuffer", which is also the answer when there is no block at all.

author: val
body: Width and height share the quadword at +0x18, stride and pixel format the one at +0x20, because the stub stores them as four 32-bit fields.

author: val
body: Version 2 of the block (cdx-to-pe.ps1 HandoffInit, 2026-08-18) adds the SMBIOS entry points the stub found in the ConfigurationTable (+0x30 the 3.0 `_SM3_` entry, +0x38 the 2.x `_SM_` one), the EDID byte count at +0x40 and up to 128 bytes of EDID at +0x48, copied from EFI_EDID_ACTIVE_PROTOCOL (or DISCOVERED when active published nothing) before ExitBootServices. A version-1 block is 48 bytes and holds none of it, so every reader below answers zero unless the version says the fields exist: a payload booted by an older stub reads "none offered", not the bytes past the block.

author: val
body: Version 3 (cdx-to-pe.ps1 GopSetLargestMode, 2026-08-20) banks what the mode selection actually did, because the guest cannot observe it any other way: the selection runs before ExitBootServices and the stage that reports it runs after, so QueryMode is gone by the time anyone could ask. Geometry alone cannot answer it either -- 1024x768 reads the same whether that was the largest mode offered or SetMode was refused.

author: val
body: +0xC8 maxmode and the mode number before the choice, +0xD0 the mode chosen and the flags, +0xD8 the EFI_STATUS SetMode answered. The block is 224 bytes.

author: val
body: A zero maxmode cannot come from a firmware that has a GOP at all, so it is the honest "the selection never ran" reading and not a real count.

author: val
body: Bit 0 says the block got past the one-mode test and ran the loop; bit 1 says SetMode was actually called. Both clear with maxmode set means the firmware offered exactly one mode. Bit 0 without bit 1 means the largest mode was already the current one, so nothing was called and the status below is the zero HandoffInit wrote rather than an answer.
